scope: M6 design exploration — Coach chat + adaptive suggestions. Design only, no app code changed. World: precision instrument + field notebook. Amber is a MARK only (never text, never button fill); amber text uses signal-ink (#8A5C12 / #F2B451). Cards: 12px radius, hairline edges, NO shadows, 12px gap within a group / 28px between sections. paper = 'act here', sunken = 'read here', one sunken well per paper card. Mobile-first, 44px targets, AA contrast, reduced-motion honoured.

wires.screen: 1. Coach entry — from the Today app (tab + sheet)
wires.notes: Two entry points, one destination. Tab: 5th item, mono label 'Coach', amber 6px mark dot above the active label (amber is a mark, never the label text). Sheet: a hairline row on Today with a mono eyebrow 'COACH' (steel), one body line, and a full-width hairline button 'Open the coach'. 44px min height both. The sheet is the escape hatch when the tab bar is busy; both deep-link to the same chat route.

wires.notes: Not bubbles, not avatars. Each turn is a labelled row separated by a hairline rule. Left gutter carries a mono eyebrow (YOU in steel; COACH in ink) + timestamp in mono steel. User text sits on the sunken surface, flush-left, body font. Coach text sits on paper with a 3px left rule — amber mark only when the answer is a live plan claim, else hairline. Below every coach answer, a sunken mini-well (the one read-here well per card) holds confidence + provenance. The 'Suggested adjustments' link is a hairline chevron row, not a CTA. Composer: hairline field + ink-filled send button (amber never fills a button).

Loading: skeleton rows in the shape of a real answer (3 lines), a static mono 'coach is thinking…' label, no spinner — a thin amber mark sweeps the left rule (reduced-motion: it stays static). Error: ink headline, one reassurance line ('Your plan and runs are safe. Nothing was changed.'), Retry as the primary ink button and Open plan as a hairline secondary. Never blame the user; never leave a half-answer on screen.

wires.notes: One suggestion per row, one sunken read-here well per card holds the count and the footer reassurance. Row anatomy: amber/hairline left rule, mono trigger eyebrow (steel, e.g. 'Missed Thu easy · 2 weeks in a row'), body proposed change in ink, one-line reason in steel. Apply = ink-filled button (44px), Dismiss = hairline ghost button. The trigger is evidence, not a command — it names what was observed in the user's own logged runs. Empty card is not rendered at all rather than shown empty.

A confirmation sheet, never a toast-and-done. Shows a Before/After diff (mono data values, aligned) so the user reads exactly what moves. Reason echoes the trigger in the user's own terms. Primary action is labelled 'Apply change' (not 'OK'), secondary 'Cancel'. Undo is promised in the footer line. No plan write happens before this tap.

The plan card keeps a permanent trace: an amber mark bar on the right edge, mono 'ADJUSTED' tag, the struck-through prior session in steel ('was Tempo run · 8.0 km'), and a sunken footer line stating when and why it changed, with Undo. Original prescriptions are never destroyed — the ledger keeps both. An applied change looks different from a hand-authored one on purpose, so the plan never quietly rewrites itself.

coach.entry: Two routes to one chat. (1) A 'Coach' item in the Today bottom nav: 5th tab, mono label, amber 6px MARK dot above the active label — amber is never the label colour. (2) A hairline sheet row on Today with a mono 'COACH' eyebrow (steel), one body line ('Ask about today's session, pacing, recovery'), and a full-width hairline button 'Open the coach'. Both deep-link to the same /coach route. 44px min targets; the tab is reachable with one thumb.
coach.messages: Row list, not bubbles and not avatars. Each turn: hairline rule above; a left gutter with a mono eyebrow (YOU = steel, COACH = ink) and a mono timestamp; body text below. User turns sit on the sunken surface (read-here) flush-left. Coach turns sit on paper with a 3px left rule — amber MARK only when the line is a live claim about the plan, hairline otherwise. Under each coach turn, one sunken mini-well holds confidence and provenance. Grouped runs of user/coach turns share tighter 12px gaps; new speaker starts a 28px section gap. Composer is a hairline field plus an ink-filled send button.
coach.grounding: A persistent single line under the chat title: 'uses your plan and logged runs', in mono steel, preceded by a small amber mark dot. It is a standing disclosure, not a tooltip, and stays visible while the user reads — so no answer is ever mistaken for general advice.
starters: Why is today a tempo run and not easy?
Am I on track for this block?
Should I rest or run today?
coach.empty: One instrument line, not a hero: 'No messages yet.' Below it, the three starter questions as tappable hairline rows (44px, chevron right). No mascot, no illustration, no 'Hi! I'm your AI coach.' The grounding line stays visible so the user knows what the coach can see.
coach.loading: Skeleton rows in the shape of a real answer (three bars) rather than a spinner, plus a static mono label 'coach is thinking…'. The answer's left rule carries a thin amber mark that sweeps once; under reduced-motion it stays a static amber mark. Composer disabled with steel placeholder. No layout jump when the real answer lands — skeletons occupy the same rows.
coach.error: Ink headline 'Couldn't reach the coach.', then reassurance in steel: 'Your plan and runs are safe. Nothing was changed.' Retry is the primary ink button; 'Open plan' is a hairline secondary. The failed user turn stays in the list; no half-written coach turn is left behind. A retry never duplicates the message. No blame language, no raw error codes.
coach.uncertainty: Confidence is always stated, never implied. High: 'Confidence: high — read from Plan W5 · 3 logged runs.' Thin evidence: 'I only have 2 logged runs, so treat this as a guess.' Missing data: 'I don't have enough to be sure — here's my read, and what would settle it.' The coach separates what it read (facts from plan/logs) from what it inferred, and when it cannot act it says so and hands off: 'I can't change your plan here — see Suggested adjustments.' Low-confidence claims drop the amber left rule and use hairline, so the mark itself signals certainty.

adjustments.card: A paper card titled 'SUGGESTED ADJUSTMENTS' with an open count in mono. Body sits in one sunken well: 'FROM YOUR LOGGED RUNS' as a mono section eyebrow, then one suggestion per row separated by hairlines, and a footer line 'Nothing changes until you apply it.' The card is only rendered when there is at least one suggestion. It never auto-applies and never nags — no badges, no red.
adjustments.row: Per row: a 3px left rule (amber MARK when evidence is strong, hairline otherwise), a mono trigger eyebrow in steel naming the observed pattern (e.g. 'Missed Thu easy · 2 weeks in a row'), the proposed change in ink body, and a one-line reason in steel. Actions on one line: Apply (ink-filled, 44px) and Dismiss (hairline ghost). The trigger cites the user's own logged data so the suggestion reads as a reading, not an order.
adjustments.apply: Apply opens a confirmation sheet — no silent write, no optimistic toast. The sheet shows a Before/After diff (mono, aligned values), the reason echoed in the user's terms, a footer 'You can undo this any time.', and two buttons: 'Cancel' (secondary) and 'Apply change' (ink primary). Only after 'Apply change' does the plan write happen. Dismiss removes the row without a confirmation and records the dismissal so the same suggestion does not immediately return.
adjustments.applied_state: On the plan, the changed session shows: an amber MARK bar on the card's right edge, a mono 'ADJUSTED' tag, the new prescription, and the prior one struck through in steel ('was Tempo run · 8.0 km · 5:12/km'). A sunken footer states provenance — 'Changed Sun 22 Nov from a coach suggestion.' — with an Undo action. The original prescription is preserved in the ledger, never overwritten. An applied change is visually distinct from a hand-authored one so the plan never appears to rewrite itself.

motion: All transitions 120–160ms ease-out, transform/opacity only; no spring, no bounce — instrument, not toy.
New coach turn enters by fading in and sliding 6px up; the left rule's amber mark draws top-to-bottom once. Reduced-motion: appears in place, mark static.
Loading skeleton uses a single slow amber-mark sweep along the answer's left rule (2s, linear). Reduced-motion: static mark, no sweep.
Confirm sheet rises from the bottom edge, 180ms ease-out; scrim fades to 40% ink. Reduced-motion: fades in place, no rise.
After 'Apply change', the plan card's 'ADJUSTED' tag and amber bar fade in (160ms) and the previous prescription's strike animates left-to-right. Reduced-motion: shown already applied.
Row removal on Dismiss collapses height 160ms then removes; reduced-motion: instant removal. Nothing moves while the user is reading.
a11y: 44px minimum touch targets on tabs, starter rows, Apply/Dismiss, composer send, and Undo.

AA contrast: body ink on paper and on sunken; steel only at 16px+ or for non-essential metadata. Amber (#E8A33D/#F2B451) is a MARK only — never text, never a button fill; amber text uses signal-ink (#8A5C12 light / #F2B451 dark).
Confidence and provenance are text, not colour: the amber left rule is redundant with the explicit 'Confidence: …' and 'Read from: …' lines.

Screen reader: each turn is a labelled group ('You, 09:12' / 'Coach, 09:12'); the grounding line is a persistent aria-describedby on the chat region; streaming text uses aria-live='polite' and the composer announces 'coach is thinking' as status, not alert.
The confirm diff is a definition list (Before / After / Reason) so it reads linearly; focus moves into the sheet on open and returns to the Apply button on close.
Error and empty states are focusable regions with a heading; Retry is the first focusable control after the message.
Reduced-motion honoured via prefers-reduced-motion for every item above; focus-visible ring uses hairline-strong, 2px, offset 2px — never amber alone.
Colour is never the sole signal: 'ADJUSTED', the strikethrough, and the provenance line all carry the meaning of an applied change without relying on the amber bar.
self_critique: Avoids the generic chat-app look: no bubbles, no avatar circles, no right-aligned gradient tails — turns are labelled instrument rows with mono eyebrows and hairline rules, matching the field-notebook world.
No purple gradients and no shadowed cards: every surface is a hairline-edged 12px-radius card; depth comes from paper vs sunken, not elevation.
Uncertainty is stated in words with a confidence line under every coach answer, so the amber mark is never the only carrier of certainty — a low-confidence answer drops to a hairline rule.

Suggestions always name their trigger from the user's logged data and require an explicit confirm with a Before/After diff; the plan shows a permanent ADJUSTED provenance trace with Undo, so the plan never silently rewrites itself.

Risk: the labelled-row format is denser and less instantly scannable than bubbles. Mitigation — 28px section gaps between speakers, the mono eyebrow gutter, and the sunken surface for user turns keep the alternation legible at a glance.

Open question for the build: whether the 5-item bottom nav crowds on small phones, and whether the Coach tab should instead collapse into the sheet when the viewport is narrow. Recommend prototyping both at 320px width before committing.
